werk/ali-farka-toure-the-river.text:
The River is an album by the Malian singer and guitarist Ali Farka Touré. It was released in January 1990 on the British label World Circuit, with Mango Records handling international distribution. Philippe Bertrand and Nick Gold produced the record. It was recorded at Studio Bolibana in Paris and at Cold Storage Studios and Garden Studios in London. Touré plays electric and acoustic guitar and the njarka, a single-string instrument. Amadou Cisse plays calabash and percussion.

The album is blues with a Malian foundation, supplemented by guest musicians. Rory McLeod plays harmonica and Steve Williamson tenor saxophone, and on "Kenouna" Seane Keane and Kevin Conneff play fiddle and bodhran. Robert Christgau gave the record an A-minus in The Village Voice and praised its uncompromising variety. The River was released in the same year as African Blues and was followed in 1993 by The Source.
werk/ali-farka-toure-the-river.listen: Listen to "Kenouna" and notice how the fiddle and bodhran sit alongside Touré's guitar.

werk/art-garfunkel-breakaway.text:
Breakaway is Art Garfunkel's second solo album. It was released on 14 October 1975 on Columbia Records. Richard Perry produced the record, except for "My Little Town", which was produced by Paul Simon, Garfunkel and Phil Ramone. The album was recorded in 1975 in Los Angeles, New York, London and Muscle Shoals, Alabama. Many session musicians took part, including Larry Knechtel, Steve Cropper and Jim Keltner.

It is soft rock with songs by Stevie Wonder, Antônio Carlos Jobim and Bruce Johnston, among others. "I Only Have Eyes for You" became Garfunkel's first number 1 in the United Kingdom. The album reached number 7 in both the United States and the United Kingdom and was certified platinum in the United States. On the Billboard 200 it thus did less well than its predecessor Angel Clare, which reached number 5.
werk/art-garfunkel-breakaway.listen: Listen to "My Little Town", a duet with Paul Simon, and notice Simon's guitar beneath the two men's harmonies.

werk/arthur-blythe-in-the-tradition.text:
In the Tradition is an album by the alto saxophonist Arthur Blythe. It was released in 1979 on Columbia Records and was his first record for that label. Blythe recorded it in New York with a quartet: Stanley Cowell on piano, Fred Hopkins on bass and Steve McCall on drums.

The record contains four jazz standards and two compositions by Blythe himself. He plays "Jitterbug Waltz" by Fats Waller, "In a Sentimental Mood" by Duke Ellington, "Caravan" by Juan Tizol and "Naima" by John Coltrane, plus his own pieces "Break Tune" and "Hip Dripper". Scott Yanow described the lineup for AllMusic as conventional and the musicians' playing as exceptionally good. AllMusic gave it four and a half stars and DownBeat, in June 1980, four. The Globe and Mail wrote that Blythe added little that was distinctive to this music.
werk/arthur-blythe-in-the-tradition.listen: Listen to "Naima", the closing track, and notice how Cowell's piano and Hopkins' bass support Blythe's alto saxophone.

werk/beyonce-4.text:
4 is Beyoncé's fourth studio album. It was released on 24 June 2011 on Parkwood Entertainment and Columbia Records. Recording ran from March 2010 to May 2011. It began with "Party" at Roc the Mic Studios in New York. Work then continued in studios in Atlanta, Los Angeles and Real World Studios in Wiltshire, among others. Producers included Beyoncé herself, Babyface, Jeff Bhasker, Kanye West, Ryan Tedder, The-Dream and Shea Taylor. The album marked her break with her father and manager Mathew Knowles.

It is a deliberately understated, mostly midtempo R&B record with influences from 1970s funk, 1980s pop and 1990s soul. Beyoncé chose to use live instruments. The record debuted at number 1 on the Billboard 200 with about 310,000 copies in its first week. In 2013 "Love On Top" won a Grammy.
werk/beyonce-4.listen: Listen to "End of Time" and notice the driving rhythm: the Afrobeat of Fela Kuti was a model for this track.

werk/beyonce-renaissance.text:
Renaissance is Beyoncé's seventh studio album and the first part of a planned trilogy. It was released on 29 July 2022 on Parkwood Entertainment and Columbia Records. She worked on it for almost three years, from 2019 and 2020, mainly in Los Angeles. Stuart White handled the vocal production and the mix. The producers include The-Dream, Nova Wav, Mike Dean, Hit-Boy, Honey Dijon, Skrillex and No I.D. Hit-Boy had already made "Thique" in 2014; the track was completed eight years later.

The album is structured as a continuous DJ mix and looks to house, disco and Black and queer club culture. Beyoncé said she had conceived it partly as a tribute to her cousin Johnny, who died during the AIDS epidemic. "Break My Soul" reached number 1 on the Hot 100. The record debuted at number 1 on the Billboard 200 and won the Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album.
werk/beyonce-renaissance.listen: Listen to "Move", the track with Grace Jones and Tems, and notice how their voices alternate with Beyoncé's.

werk/blur-the-great-escape.text:
The Great Escape is Blur's fourth studio album. It was released on 11 September 1995 on Food Records and Virgin Records. Stephen Street produced it at Maison Rouge and Townhouse in London. Damon Albarn wrote all fifteen songs. "Mr Robinson's Quango" was the first to be recorded and "It Could Be You" the last, in May 1995. The title of that last song comes from the slogan of the British National Lottery.

The record follows on from Modern Life Is Rubbish (1993) and Parklife (1994) and is regarded as the third part of that Britpop sequence. "Country House" became Blur's first number 1 in the United Kingdom in August 1995, in the Battle of Britpop against "Roll with It" by Oasis. The album topped the British album chart and was certified triple platinum. Albarn himself later called it "messy".
werk/blur-the-great-escape.listen: Listen to "Ernold Same" and notice the spoken text: the voice is that of Ken Livingstone, then a Member of Parliament.

werk/bo-diddley-have-guitar-will-travel.text:
Have Guitar, Will Travel by Bo Diddley was released in January 1960 on Checker Records in Chicago. It is his third album. The recordings were made in Chicago between 1955 and 1959, so the record collects work from several sessions. Leonard Chess, Phil Chess and Bo Diddley himself produced. Among those playing on the record are Jerome Green (maracas and vocals), Peggy Jones (guitar), Willie Dixon (bass) and Clifton James (drums).

The cover shows a white business card, modelled on the card of Paladin in the television series Have Gun – Will Travel. 'Cops and Robbers' had already been released as a single in November 1956 and was originally recorded by Boogaloo and his Gallant Crew. The Rolling Stones and George Thorogood later covered it. 'Say Man, Back Again' was released as a single in November 1959 and reached number 23 on the R&B chart. On 'Spanish Guitar' Lester Davenport plays harmonica.
werk/bo-diddley-have-guitar-will-travel.listen: Listen to 'Say Man, Back Again'. Bo Diddley and Jerome Green sing the song together and take turns talking, over a track that reached the R&B chart in 1959.

werk/bon-jovi-slippery-when-wet.text:
Slippery When Wet by Bon Jovi was released on 18 August 1986 on Mercury Records (in North America) and Vertigo Records (elsewhere). The album was recorded from January to July 1986 at Little Mountain Sound Studios in Vancouver. Bruce Fairbairn produced, and Bob Rock was the engineer and mixed it. Jon Bon Jovi and Richie Sambora wrote most of it themselves. 'You Give Love a Bad Name', 'Livin' on a Prayer', 'Without Love' and 'I'd Die for You' they wrote together with Desmond Child.

It is hard rock with choruses built for a big arena. 'You Give Love a Bad Name' and 'Livin' on a Prayer' reached number 1 on the American Billboard Hot 100, and 'Wanted Dead or Alive' number 7. The album spent eight weeks at number 1 on the Billboard 200 and, according to Billboard, was the bestselling album of 1987. The cover shows a wet black bin bag with the title drawn into it.
werk/bon-jovi-slippery-when-wet.listen: Listen to 'Livin' on a Prayer'. Richie Sambora plays the guitar riff through a talk box, and in the final chorus the song moves from E minor to G minor.

werk/brad-mehldau-places.text:
Places by Brad Mehldau was released on 5 September 2000 on Warner Bros. Mehldau recorded the album in January and March 2000 at Mad Hatter Studio in Los Angeles and produced it himself. Bernie Kirsch was the engineer. All the pieces are by Mehldau. He plays piano. Larry Grenadier (bass) and Jorge Rossy (drums) join him on six of the thirteen tracks. Mehldau plays the other pieces alone.

Each piece is named after a place, such as 'Madrid', 'Amsterdam', 'Paris' and 'Schloss Elmau'. Mehldau said that James Joyce's Ulysses influenced the structure: the album is cyclical, with a theme that opens the album and returns at the end. AllMusic gave the record four and a half stars. The Penguin Guide to Jazz gave it three stars. The reviewer David Adler called it a concept album.
werk/brad-mehldau-places.listen: Listen to 'Los Angeles' as the opener and hear the theme again in the final track, where the trio takes up the opening theme once more.

werk/carole-king-rhymes-en-reasons.text:
Rhymes & Reasons by Carole King was released in October 1972 on Ode Records. Lou Adler produced the record at A&M Studios in Hollywood, with Hank Cicalo as engineer. King sings and plays piano, clavinet, Wurlitzer and Fender Rhodes. Charles Larkey plays bass, Harvey Mason drums and Bobbye Hall percussion. Danny Kortchmar and David T. Walker play guitar. There are horns, including Harry 'Sweets' Edison on trumpet, and strings by David Campbell and Norman Kurban.

It is a pop album with horns and string arrangements. 'Been to Canaan' was the single. The song reached number 24 on the Billboard Hot 100 and topped the Adult Contemporary chart. The album reached number 2 on the American Billboard 200, number 1 in Canada and number 4 in the United Kingdom. The RIAA certified it gold. Reviewers were mixed: Rolling Stone called it 'mixed' and AllMusic gave it three out of five stars.
werk/carole-king-rhymes-en-reasons.listen: Listen to 'Ferguson Road', the only track on the record that King wrote together with Gerry Goffin. Notice how it compares with the songs she wrote alone.

werk/cassius-1999.text:
1999 is an album by the French duo Cassius, Philippe Zdar and Boombass. They wrote and produced the record themselves. The album was recorded in 1998 and released on 25 January 1999 on Virgin Records. Three singles were released: 'Cassius 1999', 'Feeling for You' and 'La Mouche'. An expanded edition adds five remixes, including 'Club 73' and a version of 'Feeling for You' by DJ Mehdi.

It is French house, built on samples from soul, funk and hip hop. 'Feeling for You' uses Al Green's 'Something', 'La Mouche' Candido's 'Thousand Finger Man' and 'Foxxy' Willie Hutch's 'Foxy Brown Theme'. AllMusic gave it four out of five stars. The album reached number 11 in France and number 28 in the United Kingdom. In September 2006 the label reported 260,000 copies sold worldwide.
werk/cassius-1999.listen: Listen to 'Feeling for You' and try to pick out the sample of Al Green's 'Something'. Also notice the drums, which come from a different song.

werk/cybotron-enter.text:
Enter is the first studio album by Cybotron, the Detroit duo of Juan Atkins and Richard '3070' Davis, formed in 1980. It was released in 1983 on Fantasy Records, with the guitarist Jon-5 (John Housely) also taking part. Atkins and Davis produced it themselves. The first pair of singles, 'Alleys of Your Mind' and 'Cosmic Raindance', came out in 1981 on Atkins' label Deep Space. 'Cosmic Cars' followed in 1982 and 'Clear' in 1983. The track list on this page is that of the 2013 reissue with extra versions of 'Cosmic Cars' and 'Techno City', among others.

The music is electro, with techno as a later consequence. AllMusic gave the album five stars. Pitchfork called it 'widely considered to be where Detroit techno began'. In 1985 Atkins left the group after creative disagreements with Davis. He started a solo career and later Metroplex. In 1990 Enter was reissued under the title Clear.
werk/cybotron-enter.listen: Listen to 'Alleys of Your Mind', the group's first single from 1981, and notice how strongly the electronic sounds and the rhythm are placed in the foreground.

werk/danny-elfman-so-lo.text:
Danny Elfman released Solo (on the cover So-Lo) in November 1984 on MCA Records. It was his first solo record. MCA had given him a solo contract when Oingo Boingo left I.R.S. Records. Recording took place in April 1983 and July 1984 at Ground Control in Santa Monica. Elfman produced with Steve Bartek and Paul Ratajczak. Most of the members of Oingo Boingo played on it, and Flea of the Red Hot Chili Peppers added extra bass.

The record is new wave with synth-pop and ska, and the tempos are slower than on the Oingo Boingo records. Elfman himself called it a chance to experiment with slower tempos. Bartek later felt that it was mainly a band record, after which Elfman persuaded MCA to transfer his contract to Oingo Boingo. "Cool City" and "Lightning" date from 1983 sessions for Good for Your Soul. The single was "Gratitude" with "Tough As Nails". Reissues appeared in 2014 and 2022.
werk/danny-elfman-so-lo.listen: Listen to Gratitude. Several mixes of this song exist (5:04, 5:12 and 4:42), so pay attention to which one you hear and whether it contains a spoken verse.

werk/dave-van-ronk-folksinger.text:
Dave Van Ronk recorded Folk Singer in April 1962 at Van Gelder Studio, with Rudy Van Gelder as engineer. Shel Kagan produced. The record was released in November 1962 on Prestige International and reissued in 1963 on Prestige Folklore. Van Ronk plays alone, on guitar and vocals. The sessions also yielded Inside Dave Van Ronk.

The album has thirteen tracks, including "Cocaine Blues", "Fixin' to Die" and "He Was a Friend of Mine". Van Ronk plays them with a jazzy touch, which makes the record folk jazz. AllMusic gave it five stars, the only Van Ronk record to receive that rating. In 2017 Pitchfork included it in a list of the two hundred best albums of the 1960s. It was his third studio album and his first for Prestige.
werk/dave-van-ronk-folksinger.listen: Listen to Cocaine Blues. There is no band: all the rhythm and harmony comes from one guitar and one voice.

werk/dexter-gordon-go.text:
Dexter Gordon recorded Go! on 27 August 1962 at Van Gelder Studio in Englewood Cliffs, with Rudy Van Gelder as engineer. Alfred Lion produced for Blue Note, on which the record was released in December 1962 as BLP 4112. Gordon plays tenor saxophone in a quartet with Sonny Clark on piano, Butch Warren on bass and Billy Higgins on drums.

It is hard bop in six tracks, together just over thirty-seven minutes long, with standards such as "Love for Sale" and "I Guess I'll Hang My Tears Out to Dry". Down Beat and AllMusic gave the record five stars. Blue Note reissued Go! in March 1999 in the RVG series, supervised by Michael Cuscuna. In 2019 the Library of Congress added the album to the National Recording Registry.
werk/dexter-gordon-go.listen: Listen to Love for Sale and notice how Gordon's tenor and Billy Higgins' rhythm together drive the record forward.

werk/diana-ross-surrender.text:
Diana Ross released Surrender on 6 July 1971 on Motown. It was her third studio album. Ashford & Simpson produced, the songwriting duo who had also overseen her self-titled debut of 1970. Paul Riser wrote all the arrangements. Several of the songs had previously been recorded by other Motown acts, such as Gladys Knight & the Pips, Martha Reeves & the Vandellas and the Four Tops.

The record is R&B and reached number 56 on the Billboard 200 and number 10 on the American R&B chart. In the United Kingdom it reached number 10. Singles were "Remember Me", "Reach Out I'll Be There" and the title track. "Remember Me" reached the American top 20 and the British top ten. The BPI certified the album silver. After "I'm Still Waiting" became a number 1 in the United Kingdom, the record was reissued under that title.
werk/diana-ross-surrender.listen: Listen to Reach Out I'll Be There, and compare Ross's version with the original by the Four Tops.

werk/dizzee-rascal-showtime.text:
Dizzee Rascal released Showtime on 6 September 2004 in the United Kingdom, on XL, and on 14 September in the United States, on Matador. He recorded the album in 2003 and 2004, as the follow-up to his debut Boy in da Corner. Besides Dizzee himself, producers included Youngstar, Cage, Taz, Vanguard and DJ Wonder.

The album is grime with hip hop and has fifteen tracks. The singles were "Stand Up Tall", "Dream" and "Off 2 Work"/"Graftin'". It reached number 8 on the British albums chart and number 1 on the independent albums chart. The BPI certified it gold. Metacritic gives it 87 out of 100, based on twenty-eight reviews, and AllMusic gave it four and a half stars. In the United States it sold less than Boy in da Corner.
werk/dizzee-rascal-showtime.listen: Listen to Dream. The track uses a sample of Happy Talk by Captain Sensible, and Dizzee raps straight across it.

werk/dizzee-rascal-the-fifth.text:
Dizzee Rascal released Fifth (on the cover The Fifth) on 30 September 2013 on Dirtee Stank Recordings and Island Records. It was his first record after his move to Universal. He recorded the album between September 2011 and April 2013, largely in Los Angeles. Producers included RedOne, will.i.am, Hi-Tek and M.J. Cole.

The record mixes hip hop, dance-leaning pop and grime, and features many guests, including Jessie J, Robbie Williams, Sean Kingston, Tinie Tempah and Bun B. Dizzee himself called it the best-produced record he had made up to that point. The album continued the experimental direction of Tongue n' Cheek (2009). Reviews were mixed, with 51 out of 100 on Metacritic. The album reached number 10 in the United Kingdom. "Goin' Crazy" was the most successful single, reaching number 5.
werk/dizzee-rascal-the-fifth.listen: Listen to Goin' Crazy and notice how Robbie Williams sings along as a guest vocalist while Dizzee raps in between.

werk/dj-snake-encore.text:
Encore is the debut album by the French producer DJ Snake. It was released on 5 August 2016 on Interscope Records. DJ Snake recorded the record between 2015 and 2016 and was executive producer himself. He worked with Skrillex, Mike Dean, Andrew Watt and Louis Bell, among others. Many tracks feature a guest singer or rapper, including Justin Bieber, Travis Scott, Migos, Young Thug and Jeremih.

The music lies between EDM and trap. Five singles were released from the album: Middle, Propaganda, Talk, Let Me Love You and The Half. Encore entered at number 8 on the Billboard 200, DJ Snake's first top-ten album, and topped the American chart for dance and electronic albums. In the United States the record was certified platinum. Reviews were mixed to positive: Rolling Stone gave three out of five stars and felt that the guests were given too little room.
werk/dj-snake-encore.listen: Listen to Middle, the first single, and notice how Bipolar Sunshine's vocal keeps floating above the bass and synthesizers, without the track erupting into a hard drop.

werk/emma-bunton-a-girl-like-me.text:
A Girl Like Me is the first solo album by Emma Bunton, one of the Spice Girls. It was released on 16 April 2001 on Virgin Records, after the Spice Girls had stopped recording in 2000. Bunton recorded the record between July 1999 and October 2000 in Dublin, London, Stockholm and Los Angeles, among other places. Producers included Steve Mac, Richard "Biff" Stannard, Julian Gallagher and Tin Tin Out. Bunton wrote most of the lyrics.

It is a pop album with influences from R&B and dance. There are two covers on it: Sunshine on a Rainy Day and What I Am, which Bunton recorded with Tin Tin Out. What Took You So Long? became her first number 1 in the United Kingdom. The album reached number 4 on the British albums chart and was certified gold by the BPI. Critics praised the songs but found the production lacking in character. In 2002 Bunton left Virgin.
werk/emma-bunton-a-girl-like-me.listen: Listen to What I Am and notice how Bunton and Tin Tin Out turn the song by Edie Brickell & New Bohemians into a danceable pop version.

werk/eurythmics-touch.text:
Touch is the third studio album by Eurythmics, the British duo of Annie Lennox and David A. Stewart. It was released on 14 November 1983 on RCA Records. Stewart produced the record, with Jon Bavin as engineer. The duo recorded and mixed the album in about three weeks at The Church, their own studio in London. Dick Cuthell played trumpet and flugelhorn, and Dean Garcia bass. Michael Kamen wrote the string arrangements for the British Philharmonic Orchestra.

Touch is synth-pop with touches of new wave. The three singles, Who's That Girl?, Right by Your Side and Here Comes the Rain Again, all reached the British top ten. It became the duo's first number 1 album in the United Kingdom and reached number 7 on the Billboard 200. The album was certified platinum in the United Kingdom and the United States, and gold in the Netherlands. In 2012 Rolling Stone ranked it number 492 on its list of the 500 greatest albums.
werk/eurythmics-touch.listen: Listen to Here Comes the Rain Again and notice Michael Kamen's pizzicato strings, set against the programmed drums and sequencers.

werk/george-michael-faith.text:
Faith is George Michael's first solo album. It was released on 30 October 1987 in the United States on Columbia Records and on 2 November in the United Kingdom on Epic Records. Michael wrote and produced the record himself. Only Look at Your Hands he wrote together with David Austin. He recorded the album between August 1986 and September 1987 at Puk Studios in Denmark and Sarm West Studios in London. He played many of the instruments himself, including the Yamaha DX7 and the LinnDrum.

Faith mixes pop, funk, soul and rock. Seven singles were released from it. Four of them, Faith, Father Figure, One More Try and Monkey, reached number 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. The album spent twelve weeks at the top of the Billboard 200 and won the Grammy for Album of the Year. The RIAA certified it Diamond. In 2020 Rolling Stone ranked it number 151 on its list of the 500 greatest albums.
werk/george-michael-faith.listen: Listen to Faith and notice the opening: a church organ, followed by strummed guitar and handclaps on the Bo Diddley beat of a LinnDrum loop.

werk/george-shearing-bossa-nova.text:
Shearing Bossa Nova is an album by the British pianist George Shearing, who was born in London and had been an American citizen since 1956. He recorded it from 17 to 19 December 1962 for Capitol Records, on which it was released in 1963. Tom Morgan produced. Clare Fischer wrote the arrangements and conducted. Besides Shearing, you hear woodwinds and a Brazilian rhythm section.

The repertoire consists of bossa nova and jazz standards. Shearing plays Brazilian pieces such as One Note Samba, Desafinado and Manhã de Carnaval, but also On Green Dolphin Street and Come Rain or Come Shine. Samba da Borboleta and Pensativa are by Fischer. Shearing recorded for Capitol until 1969 and made more Latin records in those years, such as Latin Affair (1960) and Mood Latino (1961). AllMusic gave the album four out of five stars and named Samba da Borboleta and Pensativa as highlights.
werk/george-shearing-bossa-nova.listen: Listen to Pensativa and notice how Shearing plays the melody on piano while Fischer's arrangement places woodwinds and a Brazilian rhythm around it.

werk/golden-earring-together.text:
Together is the eighth studio album by the Dutch rock band Golden Earring. It was released on 16 June 1972 on Polydor. The lineup consisted of Barry Hay (vocals, flute, saxophone, guitar), George Kooymans (guitar, vocals), Rinus Gerritsen (bass guitar, keyboards) and Cesar Zuiderwijk (drums). The band recorded the album in March 1972 at Island Studios in London. Fred Haayen produced. Kooymans wrote all the songs, except Cruisin' Southern Germany by Hay. The album was not released in the United States.

The music is hard rock with progressive elements. The album has eight tracks, of which Brother Wind, at 7:54, is the longest. The single Buddy Joe was released in April 1972 and reached number 3 in the Netherlands, number 5 in Belgium and number 12 in Germany. The album itself reached number 6 on the Dutch Album Top 100 and number 33 in Germany. AllMusic gave it three out of five stars.
werk/golden-earring-together.listen: Listen to Brother Wind (7:54) and Cruisin' Southern Germany (3:00) back to back and notice how much room the band allows itself in each track: Barry Hay sings both, but one lasts almost three times as long as the other.

werk/grace-jones-fame.text:
Grace Jones released the album Fame in 1978, which appears as The Fame in streaming catalogues. It is her second studio album. Island Records released it on 7 June 1978. The producer Tom Moulton recorded it in 1977 and 1978 at Sigma Sound Studios in Philadelphia. John Davis handled the arrangements and played keyboards, Jimmy Williams played bass and Keith Benson drums.

It is a disco record. Side A is one continuous medley of "Do or Die", "Pride" and "Fame", together almost nineteen minutes long. "Do or Die" became a club hit in the United States and Canada. The album reached number 97 on the American Billboard 200 and number 5 on the Canadian dance chart of RPM. AllMusic gives it three out of five stars.
werk/grace-jones-fame.listen: Listen to the start of side A: "Do or Die", "Pride" and "Fame" flow into one another without a pause, as in a club set. Try to hear where one track ends and the next begins.

werk/inspiral-carpets-life.text:
Life is the debut album by Inspiral Carpets. It was released on 23 April 1990 on Mute Records, through the band's own label Cow Records. The band recorded it in September 1989 at Out of the Blue and produced it themselves, together with Nick Garside. The lineup consisted of singer Tom Hingley, organist Clint Boon, guitarist Graham Lambert, bassist Martyn Walsh and drummer Craig Gill.

The record belongs to Madchester: guitar music with a distinct role for the organ. "This Is How It Feels" reached number 14 on the British singles chart and "She Comes in the Fall" number 27. In 1990 the album reached number 2 on the British albums chart and was certified gold by the BPI. "Move" appears on the British CD and cassette as a bonus track. The Beast Inside followed in 1991.
werk/inspiral-carpets-life.listen: In "This Is How It Feels", listen to Clint Boon's organ alongside Graham Lambert's guitar. Notice how those two instruments together fill out the band's sound.

werk/katy-perry-one-of-the-boys.text:
One of the Boys is Katy Perry's second studio album and the first under that name. Capitol Records released it on 17 June 2008. Perry had been working on it since she was eighteen, with Greg Wells, Dr. Luke, Glen Ballard, Dave Stewart and Butch Walker, among others, as producers. The sessions ran through fifteen studios in Los Angeles, New York, Surrey and Glasgow. Her earlier record Katy Hudson (2001) was a Christian rock album.

The album is pop music with rock and power pop influences. Four singles entered the American Hot 100: "I Kissed a Girl" reached number 1, "Hot n Cold" number 3, "Waking Up in Vegas" number 9 and "Thinking of You" number 29. The album debuted at number 9 on the Billboard 200 and is certified triple platinum in the United States. Critical reception was mixed: Metacritic gives it 47 out of 100.
werk/katy-perry-one-of-the-boys.listen: Listen to the chorus of "Hot n Cold". The lyrics set opposites side by side to describe a partner's changing moods. Count how many pairs you hear.

werk/king-crimson-red.text:
Red is King Crimson's seventh studio album. Island Records released it on 7 October 1974, and in North America it came out on Atlantic. The band produced it themselves. The studio parts were recorded in July and August 1974 at Olympic Studios in Barnes, London. Only "Providence" was recorded live, on 30 June 1974 in Providence, Rhode Island. The core of the band consisted of Robert Fripp, John Wetton and Bill Bruford. Fripp disbanded the group in September 1974, shortly before the release.

The record is prog rock with heavy guitars and bass. In 1974 it made little impact: number 45 in Great Britain, for one week, and number 66 in the United States. Later reviews are very positive, with Pitchfork giving 9.0 out of 10. In 2024 a 50th Anniversary Edition was released with an elemental mix by David Singleton. This track listing comes from that mix and does not include "Providence".
werk/king-crimson-red.listen: Listen to "Red". The opening motif returns at the end. In the middle, bass and drums drive along a heavily accented, syncopated figure.

werk/nine-inch-nails-the-fragile.text:
The Fragile is the third studio album by Nine Inch Nails. Nothing Records and Interscope Records released it on 21 September 1999 as a double album with a left and a right disc. Trent Reznor produced it with Alan Moulder, who also mixed it. Recording lasted from January 1997 to July 1999 and took place at Nothing Studios in New Orleans. Reznor played most of it himself. Charlie Clouser, Danny Lohner, Jerome Dillon, Adrian Belew, Mike Garson and Bill Rieflin, among others, contributed to a few tracks.

Reznor described the album as a sequel to The Downward Spiral (1994). It sounds less harsh: industrial rock and art rock, with ambient and electronica. On release it entered at number 1 on the American Billboard 200, with 229,000 copies in its first week, and it is certified double platinum in the United States. Reviewers praised the ambition and criticised the length. Things Falling Apart followed in 2000.
werk/nine-inch-nails-the-fragile.listen: Listen to "The Day the World Went Away". The song has no drums and builds on one repeated melodic line. Notice the transition from the dense, heavy layer of guitars to the sparser passage with piano and a clear singing voice.

werk/portishead-third.text:
Third is Portishead's third studio album and their first in eleven years, after Portishead of 1997. Island Records released it in the United Kingdom on 28 April 2008. In the United States it came out a day later on Mercury. The band produced it themselves and recorded it between 2005 and 2008 in their own studios in Bristol. Beth Gibbons sings, Geoff Barrow plays drums, synthesizers and bass, among other instruments, and Adrian Utley plays guitar, ukulele and keyboards.

The album leaves the trip hop of the earlier records behind. It sounds like experimental rock with electronics. In the United Kingdom it reached number 2, in the Netherlands number 8 and in the United States number 7, the band's highest American debut. Metacritic gives it 85 out of 100. "Machine Gun", "The Rip" and "Magic Doors" were released as singles.
werk/portishead-third.listen: Listen to "Machine Gun" and notice the beat that carries the track. It was later sampled by The Weeknd in "Belong to the World". Hear how hard and mechanical it sounds against the voice of Beth Gibbons.

werk/siouxsie-and-the-banshees-juju.text:
Juju is an album by Siouxsie and the Banshees, released on 19 June 1981 by Polydor. The group recorded it in March 1981 at Surrey Sound in Leatherhead, Surrey. Nigel Gray produced it together with the band. The lineup consisted of Siouxsie Sioux (vocals), Steven Severin (bass guitar), Budgie (drums and percussion) and John McGeoch (guitar).

Two singles preceded the album: "Spellbound" on 22 May 1981 and "Arabian Knights" on 24 July 1981. In the United Kingdom Juju reached number 7 on the albums chart and was awarded a silver disc by the BPI, for 60,000 copies. Sounds gave it 4.5 stars. Paul Morley wrote in the NME that it was the first integrated Banshees album since The Scream. The 2006 CD reissue adds bonus tracks, including 12" versions of two singles.
werk/siouxsie-and-the-banshees-juju.listen: Compare "Spellbound" with the 12" mix at track 10: the extended version lasts 4:41, the album version 3:20.

werk/thad-jones-after-hours.text:
After Hours is an album by the trumpeter Thad Jones, released in 1957 by Prestige (PR 7118). It was recorded on 21 June 1957 at Rudy Van Gelder's studio in Hackensack, New Jersey. Bob Weinstock supervised. Besides Jones, the players are Frank Wess (flute and tenor saxophone), Mal Waldron (piano), Kenny Burrell (guitar), Paul Chambers (bass) and Art Taylor (drums). The album is credited to the Prestige All Stars, with Jones as nominal leader.

All four tracks are by Mal Waldron. They last from almost eight to well over twelve minutes: "Empty Street" runs to 12:35. It is bop in the straight-ahead tradition, recorded in a single session. AllMusic gave it four out of five stars and wrote that the lineup is in good form. The Penguin Guide to Jazz Recordings gave it three out of four stars.
werk/thad-jones-after-hours.listen: In "Steamin'", listen to the front line: Jones' trumpet alongside Frank Wess on flute or tenor saxophone, with Kenny Burrell's guitar in the rhythm section.

werk/cannonball-adderley-in-the-land-of-.text:
In the Land of Hi-Fi with Julian Cannonball Adderley is an album by the alto saxophonist Cannonball Adderley, released in 1956 by EmArcy (MG 36077). It was recorded on 8 and 18 June 1956 at Capitol Studios in New York. The lineup is a nonet: Adderley, his brother Nat (cornet), Ernie Royal (trumpet), Bobby Byrne and Jimmy Cleveland (trombone), Jerome Richardson (tenor saxophone and flute), Danny Bank (baritone saxophone), Junior Mance (piano), Keter Betts (bass) and Specs Wright (drums). Ernie Wilkins conducted and arranged.

It is hard bop in arrangements for six horns. Wilkins wrote the opening track "Dog My Cats". There are also standards, such as "Little Girl Blue" by Rodgers and Hart, and original material from within the group: "Blues for Bohemia" by the Adderley brothers and "Junior's Tune" by Mance. No track lasts much longer than four minutes. The album followed Julian Cannonball Adderley and Strings (1955). AllMusic gave it 2.5 stars, the Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide (1985) three.
werk/cannonball-adderley-in-the-land-of-.listen: In "Dog My Cats", which lasts only 2:26, listen to how Ernie Wilkins sets the six horns as a single block against Adderley's alto saxophone.

werk/herbie-hancock-maiden-voyage.text:
Maiden Voyage is Herbie Hancock's fifth album as a leader, released on 17 May 1965 by Blue Note. It was recorded on 17 March 1965 at Rudy Van Gelder's studio in Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey. Alfred Lion produced. Besides Hancock (piano), the players are Freddie Hubbard (trumpet), George Coleman (tenor saxophone), Ron Carter (bass) and Tony Williams (drums). Hancock, Coleman, Carter and Williams had shortly before played together in Miles Davis's quintet.

It is modal jazz and post-bop, conceived as a record about the sea. Many titles refer to water or sea creatures, and the group builds the atmosphere mainly through space. The title track, "The Eye of the Hurricane" and "Dolphin Dance" became jazz standards. The Penguin Guide to Jazz includes the record in its Core Collection. AllMusic called it perhaps Hancock's best of the 1960s. In 1999 the album received a Grammy Hall of Fame Award.
werk/herbie-hancock-maiden-voyage.listen: In "Dolphin Dance", listen to the melody: Hancock says that Count Basie's "Shiny Stockings" was the main inspiration.
